rationale: Start with a broad gradient to locate the elution window and critical pairs while minimizing the risk of missing strongly retained compounds. A 10-minute gradient at moderate temperature provides a baseline for targeted window, slope, and temperature optimization.

Change only gradient duration to determine whether the crowded early cluster separates with a shallower slope. This also measures the late pair’s slope response before optimizing temperature and trimming the gradient window.

Test temperature selectivity against injection 1 while keeping the gradient unchanged. Higher temperature may separate the early cluster and shorten retention without the time penalty of a longer gradient.

Retain the favorable temperature selectivity and use a shallower gradient to improve the sole under-resolved pair. The last peak should remain below 10 minutes, giving this method a chance to reach the maximum CRF.

The remaining critical pair worsened with a shallower gradient, so test a higher starting organic fraction to shift its selectivity rather than lengthening the run. Keep the favorable 60 C temperature and ample final solvent strength.

Increase the starting organic fraction one more step to extend the improvement in the remaining critical pair. The neighboring pair has some resolution margin, and the first peak should remain sufficiently retained to test this adjustment.

Injection 6 reached the maximum CRF; now shorten the gradient one step to seek a faster fully resolved method. Keep the solvent window and temperature fixed to isolate the effect on the two closest pairs.

Narrow the gradient window to recover resolution for the two marginal pairs at the shorter duration. This slope lies between injections 6 and 7 and should retain full resolution while eluting the last peak sooner than injection 6.

Test whether another step upward in starting organic fraction can shorten the fully resolved method from injection 8. Monitor the early cluster and first peak closely, since reduced initial retention may offset the selectivity gain.

The maximum score is already secured, so test the opposite temperature extreme for an alternative selectivity regime. Comparing directly with injections 1 and 3 will reveal whether the crowded cluster separates after further elution-order changes.

Return to the successful 60 C selectivity and test a six-minute gradient with a narrower solvent window. Its slope is slightly steeper than injection 8, probing whether full resolution can be retained with earlier final elution.

Test whether a small temperature reduction can rebalance the two marginal early pairs in the faster method from injection 7. Injection 11 still has a pair below 1.5 despite its rounded CRF, so injection 8 remains the fastest confirmed fully resolved method.

Keep 60 C and flatten injection 9’s gradient to improve its single under-resolved early pair. This tests whether the higher starting organic fraction can yield another maximum-score method with a different balance of critical-pair resolutions.

Lower injection 11’s endpoint one step to bring its marginal pair above R = 1.5 while retaining the six-minute gradient. The last peak should elute near the gradient end, with slightly more resolution margin than injection 8.

Flatten injection 13’s gradient another step to lift its sole critical pair above R = 1.5. This tests an alternative fully resolved method with potentially greater resolution margin while keeping the last peak below 10 minutes.

With maximum CRF secured, test a shallower gradient at the successful starting composition to increase critical-pair resolution margins. The last peak should remain below 10 minutes, potentially providing a less marginal maximum-score method.

Test the remaining endpoint step between fully resolved injection 8 and faster but under-resolved injection 7. This directly checks whether the fastest confirmed maximum-score method can be shortened further without losing full resolution.

Back off the slope to provide more resolution margin than injection 8 while remaining faster than injection 16. Injection 17 establishes that further steepening sacrifices full resolution, so this tests a nearby maximum-score operating point.

Refine between injections 18 and 16 to improve the critical-pair margin without extending the last peak as far as 7.66 minutes. This should preserve the maximum CRF while providing a less marginal alternative to the fastest fully resolved method, injection 8.
